newsitem.title: DUBAI: EU seeks bigger role in Mideast peace process.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks bigger role in Mideast peace process.

text.p: France and Britain are eager to establish a bigger European role in the Middle East peace process, but their efforts are hampered by policy differences in the EU, the head of a European pressure group said on Tuesday.
"The European Union is not as united as the United States of America," Jean-Michel Dumont, secretary general of the Parliamentary Association for Euro-Arab Cooperation told Reuters.
"What is agreed to at EU parliament level does not commit parliaments of the member states," said Dumont, whose association represents 97 seats at the 626-seat EU parliament.
He said the EU in general and France in particular played a major role in realising an April 26 U.S.-sponsored understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
"We wish for this role to continue on a larger scale," said Dumont, who is on a visit to the UAE to organise a three-day conference in April on the Middle East Peace process.
The United States has been the main peace sponsor in the Middle East since the launch of the peace process in Madrid in 1991.

Dumont said a recent Middle East tour by EU envoy Miguel Angeles Moratinos aimed at relaunching Israeli-Syrian talks, which were broken off last March when a Labour government was still in power in the Jewish state.

Syria says the Labour government, which lost to Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party in elections last May, agreed to withdraw from the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Negotiations have not resumed under Netanyahu, who rejects trading Arab land for peace. Syria insists it will resume talks if they begin where the last round left off.
Moratinos' trip, which included Egypt and Israel, was his second to the region since he was named EU envoy to the Middle East to boost Europe's role in the peace negotiations.
